tour.name: Bangkok Private Tour: Grand Palace & Emerald Buddha, Wat Pho, Wat Arun & a Khlong Boat
tour.subtitle: A private day in royal Bangkok with a licensed guide and car: the Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, the giant reclining Buddha of Wat Pho, a Thai lunch by the river, a long-tail boat through the canals of Thonburi and sunset at Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn.

tour.overview:
In 1782 King Rama I moved the capital of Siam across the Chao Phraya river to a small trading post called Bangkok and began building the Grand Palace on the island of Rattanakosin. Two hundred years later, Bangkok is a megacity of more than ten million people, but its royal heart, with its golden spires, glittering temples and canals, remains the soul of Thailand.

This private day shows royal Bangkok with a licensed guide and a car, so you avoid the heat, the traffic and the scams that target visitors outside the palace. You visit the Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha at opening time, see the reclining Buddha of Wat Pho, the birthplace of Thai massage, have lunch by the river, then take a private long-tail boat through the canals, the khlongs, of Thonburi, where wooden houses on stilts still line the water, and end at Wat Arun.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bangkok
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car, driver and long-tail boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 5 km on flat ground, in the heat

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew.
• Wat Pho and the reclining Buddha.
• The Chao Phraya river.
• The khlongs of Thonburi by long-tail boat.
• Wat Arun.

WHY THIS WORKS
We arrive at the Grand Palace at 8:30 opening, before the heat and the tour buses, and use the river and canals instead of the traffic in the afternoon.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Bangkok, families and anyone who wants to understand Thai Buddhism and the monarchy.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want markets and rural life, choose our floating market and railway market tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Grand Palace has a strict dress code: long trousers or skirts and covered shoulders for everyone; no sandals without straps. Ignore anyone outside the palace who says it is closed: it is a well-known scam.

days.name: The Grand Palace and Emerald Buddha, Wat Pho, lunch by the river, a khlong boat and Wat Arun
days.description:
What to expect: the royal and religious heart of Bangkok with a licensed guide, private car, tickets, a long-tail boat and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 8:00 and drive to Rattanakosin island for the 8:30 opening of the Grand Palace. Inside its white walls, nearly two kilometres long, you first visit Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha. The small statue, carved from a single block of green jade or jasper, is the palladium of the kingdom; the king himself changes its golden robes three times a year, for the hot, rainy and cool seasons. Around it, golden chedis, mythical guardian giants and the murals of the Ramakien, the Thai version of the Ramayana, cover the cloisters. You then see the throne halls of the palace, among them the Chakri Maha Prasat, a European-style building crowned with Thai roofs, built in 1882.

A short drive brings you to Wat Pho, the oldest and largest temple of Bangkok. Its reclining Buddha is 46 metres long and 15 metres high, covered in gold leaf, with mother-of-pearl soles showing 108 auspicious symbols. Wat Pho was Thailand's first university and is the home of traditional Thai massage; you can end the visit with a 30-minute massage in its school if you wish.

Lunch is at a restaurant on the river, with a view of Wat Arun – green curry, pad thai, tom yum soup and mango sticky rice. In the afternoon you board a private long-tail boat at the pier and turn into the khlongs of Thonburi, the 'Venice of the East', where wooden houses on stilts, small temples and orchid gardens line the water and vendors paddle by. The boat drops you at Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, whose central prang, more than 70 metres tall, is decorated with pieces of Chinese porcelain and seashells. You climb its steep steps for a view over the river as the light turns golden, then your driver takes you back to your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:30 – Grand Palace and the Emerald Buddha (about 2 hours).
11:00 – Wat Pho and the reclining Buddha.
12:30 – Lunch by the river.
14:00 – Long-tail boat in the Thonburi canals.
15:15 – Wat Arun.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Grand Palace may close at short notice for royal ceremonies; we then visit Wat Benchamabophit, the Marble Temple, instead.
• A Thai massage at the Wat Pho school can be added.
• The weather is hot and humid all year; we carry cold water and towels.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun tickets, private long-tail boat, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Thai massage, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: What is the dress code?
faq.answer: At the Grand Palace and temples, everyone must cover shoulders and knees: long trousers or long skirts, sleeved tops, and no see-through clothes. Wraps can be bought or borrowed at the entrance.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Grand Palace with Wat Phra Kaew, Wat Pho and Wat Arun, plus the private boat.

faq.question: Someone told us the palace is closed today. Is that true?
faq.answer: Almost certainly not: it is a common scam to redirect visitors to gem shops. Your guide meets you and takes you straight in.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a Thai lunch by the river. Your guide adapts the spice level, and vegetarian and other diets are easy.

faq.question: Is it very hot?
faq.answer: Bangkok is hot and humid all year. We start early, use the air-conditioned car between sites and carry cold water and towels.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the guardian giants, the huge Buddha and the boat. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The palace and Wat Pho are flat; boarding the long-tail boat needs a step down, and Wat Arun's steps are steep but optional.

faq.question: Will we be taken to gem or tailor shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required; a small amount for your guide and driver is customary if you were happy.

faq.question: Can we add a Thai massage?
faq.answer: Yes, at the massage school of Wat Pho, the home of traditional Thai massage, for about 30 or 60 minutes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to February is the coolest and driest. March to May is very hot; June to October brings afternoon showers.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
